open_obligations: Note the different information condition: Khan et al.'s judges see no passage, Parrish et al.'s have 90 s of access.
Check that the naive baseline (60%) is comparable to Parrish et al.'s passage-only condition.
Check the human judge filtering (21 judges after filtering) for selection effects.
in.other_title: Human judges 88% with debate vs 78% consultancy; LLM judges 76% vs 54% (naive 60% / 48%)
in.rationale: Parrish et al. say their null result is a limited case study, not evidence against debate. Khan et al. report non-expert human judges reach 88% with debate between persuasive LLM debaters versus 60% naive and 78% consultancy on QuALITY HARD; their judges cannot read the story and see verified quotes, and debates run for 3 rounds.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether a debate set-up can help non-expert judges on QuALITY when the single-turn human-argument null result is not the whole story

text: The authors state that the current study is limited in scope and is not strong evidence against the broad potential usefulness of a debate-style set-up; the experiments are a case study of a scenario where humans cannot be sure of the answer but have access to evidence to help identify it.
title: Single-turn debate null result is a limited case study, not evidence against debate
